plan.title: Outside or treadmill? An important unknown is asked, not assumed

context.text: either outside or the treadmill in my building's gym, depends on the weather
Got it. Do you track your runs with anything?
my apple watch tracks it all
Nice, the watch makes proof easy. Anything you're working toward, like a distance or a race?

transcript.text: not really, just want more stamina

Stamina is a great goal, Taylor, and 20 minutes of steady running is the way to build it. Here's the plan:
• Headed for: more running stamina
• Today: 20 minute easy run at 6 pm, outside if it's dry, otherwise the treadmill. Keep a pace where you could still talk, and walk breaks are fine.
• Schedule: 6 pm, 20 minutes, Mon, Wed, Fri, Sat
• Proof: a screenshot of your Apple Watch workout summary. It's easy, and it keeps us honest.
• Why: steady, easy runs are how stamina builds, and rest days let your legs adapt.

Each run shapes the next one, so we'll build toward longer stretches without running too hard. What do you think?

Treadmill it is, good call with the rain. Here's the updated plan:
• Headed for: more running stamina
• Today: 20 minute easy run at 6 pm on the building gym treadmill. Keep a pace where you could still talk, and walk breaks are fine.
• Schedule: 6 pm, 20 minutes, Mon, Wed, Fri, Sat (outside on dry days, treadmill otherwise)
• Proof: a screenshot of your Apple Watch workout summary
• Why: steady, easy runs build stamina, and the rest days let your legs adapt.

Each run shapes the next one, so we build up gradually. What do you think?
Taylor, glad it works for you. Are you committing to this plan, starting with the treadmill run today at 6 pm?
